"State cannot adopt discriminatory provisions of schooling to cater to different groups using public funds as it would violate the basic principles of equality and social justice," contended the PIL filed by Social Jurist, an NGO based in Delhi.

Advocate Ashok Agarwal, the petitioner's counsel, submitted that using public finds, the state had to provide schools of comparable quality to all the children who seek education through state or state-supported schools.

Seeking replies from the Ministry of HRD and all the state governments, the court also sought a response as to why so far Article 21-A (right to education) had not been enforced. Agarwal essentially sought a direction for enforcement of the Fundamental Right to Elementary Education.

The PIL also brought out the deplorable state of elementary education in India, with a large number of schools lacking both academic and physical infrastructure, resulting in large-scale dropouts among children in the age group of 6-14 years.

The state had failed to provide good quality education to all the children, especially those belonging to backward classes and minorities, the petition further stated.

Heading: BJP worker arrested for illegal firearms trade - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Mayawati Government "to look afresh" into its earlier decision of cancelling the allotment of land to several hotel companies that were allotted properties by UP's previous Government under Mulayam Singh Yadav. The decision, however, echoes a similar one made by the Allahabad High Court and has left the hoteliers frustrated.

The companies that approached the court, including ITC and Indian Hotels Company Ltd, had been leased land for building 14 hotels in Noida ahead of the Commonwealth Games in 2006. However, Mayawati, alleging corruption in land auctions, canceled the allotments.

When the hoteliers challenged the cancellation in Allahabad High Court, it remanded the matter to the state Government for reconsideration. The hotel companies then moved the Supreme Court in hopes of a more definitive judgment in their favour.

The bench headed by Justice R V Raveendran issued notice to the state Government and the Noida Authority and also directed both parties to maintain the status quo with regard to dispossessing the allottees. The companies will present their case on August 11 before Principle Secretary, Industrial Development Department, UP. The court added that the fresh hearing should be uninfluenced by the Allahabad HC, which had criticised the earlier state Government of violating the Master Plan.

Senior advocate Harish Salve told the court that industry status does not imply that the rules of an industrial zone have to be followed. The apex court has scheduled a further hearing for the case on September 9.

Heading: One dead in Sikh-Dera clash, curfew imposed in Haryana town - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police has arrested Vikrant Ramesh Chandwadkar, a weapons dealer and a national-level tour manager of the BJP, for his alleged involvement in an illegal firearms trade. Chandwadkar was arrested at his residence in Nashik on Thursday.

He was implicated when a crime branch team led by inspector Vijaysinh Gaikwad nabbed Sachin Sudam Beldare at Narpatgiri chowk for being in possession of a sophisticated German-made revolver and a fake licence on Tuesday afternoon. According to a senior crime branch officer, further investigations revealed that the revolver and licence originated from Viraj Armoury in Nashik, a shop owned by Chandwadkar. The fake licence was then tracked back to Nashik-based Radhacharan Jamnaprasad Nayak who had procured it from J-K.

Suspecting that both Chandwadkar and Nayak are involved in a fake licence racket and illegal firearms trade, police arrested both on Thursday. They were booked under sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the IPC and remanded to police custody till July 25.

Meanwhile, Vikrant Chandwadkar's father, Ramesh Chandwadkar, suspects that his son's arrest is part of a political conspiracy. "The BJP had asked Vikrant to help transport MP Harishchandra Chavan to Nashik for the trust vote on June 22. Chavan cannot walk, so Vikrant was supposed to take him in a special plane. Chavan's absence could prove to be a major loss for the party. So there is possibility of a conspiracy to arrest Vikrant in order to create hurdles in taking Chavan to Delhi," he said.

Heading: Power cuts lead to water crisis in AP - Indian Express
Content:
Curfew was imposed in a town of Haryana's Sirsa district on Friday morning following clashes between Sikhs and Dera Sacha Sauda followers that left one person dead and several injured.

The two groups clashed over an ongoing naam charcha (religious discourse) at the house of a Dera follower in Dabwali.

Later in the evening, police registered a case of murder and arrested a Dera follower, Sunder Das.

Sources in the police said that another Dera follower, Ram Gopal, was also rounded up in connection with the case.

Earlier in the day, a group of irate Sikhs hit the thoroughfares of Dabwali, vandalising shops and houses belonging to Dera followers after one Harmander Singh (30) died after being allegedly thrashed by Dera followers around 7 am.

Harmander Singh, a member of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar Sabha, had reportedly gone with a few others, to the house of Sunder Das for stalling the ongoing naam charcha at the latter's house.

When the news of Harmander Singh's death spread, a large number of Sikhs, brandishing swords, lathis and other weapons, went on the rampage across the town. Raising anti-Dera slogans, they set some 40 shops on fire as cops remained a mute spectator to the violence. A few houses and two-wheelers parked on roads were also set ablaze. Several fire tenders were pressed into service to contain the fire.

A few cops posted at Dabwali police station too, sustained injuries after the police party was pelted with stones. Sirsa Deputy Commissioner V Umashankar, who reached the spot and tried to pacify the mob, also sustained minor injuries.

The district administration, in order to control the situation, imposed curfew in the town around 1:30 pm.

While Sirsa DC V Umashankar and SP Venkat Raman reached the town, the police forces took long to arrive. Dabwali, however, turned into a police cantonment later in the day after police and other forces arrived in huge numbers and carried out flag marches.

Takht Damdama Sahib chief Balwant Singh Nandgarh reached Dabwali soon after learning about the incident. "This is all being done at the behest of Dera chief. He should be booked in the case under Sections 120-B (of IPC)," Nandgarh said.

Khalsa Action Committee (KAC) member and Sikh religious figure Baba Baljit Singh Daduwal also reached Dabwali to offer his condolences to the family of deceased. "As the law is tightening its noose around Dera chief in different cases, the latter has instructed his followers to attack Sikhs when they try to stop naam charcha," Daduwal said.

SGPC president Avtar Singh Makkar also reached Dabwali later in the day.

Heading: Centre to take steps to stop attacks on TN fishermen - Indian Express
Content:
Power shortage in Andhra Pradesh has started affecting water supply in several cities and towns, including Hyderabad. The crisis has also led to an acute shortage of diesel as the demand has gone up due to increased use of generators.

Hyderabad is reeling under drinking water shortage with residential areas in the heart of the city and suburbs receiving water once in two days.

However, the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB), which supplies 290 million gallons of water per day, claimed there is no water shortage. "We can still maintain the required water supply. But several areas are not receiving water as there is no power at the nearest pumping stations during the regular supply time. Hence, the supply has become erratic. Areas where there is no power crisis receive adequate supply at the specified time," said Director (Technical) Prabhakar Sharma.

"We are receiving several complaints daily. But we are not at fault. How can we pump water when there is no power?" said an irate HMWSSB official. "On a rotation basis, different areas of the city have two- to three-hour long power cuts at different times. Many residential areas face power cuts at the time of water supply, and if there is no power at the pumping station, the areas do not get water," said the official.

The HMWSSB is preparing a contingency plan in case rains fail and levels in water sources fall.

Hyderabad sources drinking water from the Nagarjuna Sagar, and rivers Musi and Manjira. The state Government is also speeding up work on the second phase of the Krishna Drinking Water Supply Phase II. "The project is 75 per cent complete, but we can still start supplying water from this project," Sharma says.

Union Finance Minister

P Chidambaram will inaugurate the project at Sahebnagar near Nagarjuna Sagar highway on Saturday.

Meanwhile, many petrol pumps in the city have run out of diesel stock due to a sudden increase in the demand. Pump owners said that power cuts have forced small industries and business establishments to use diesel generators, which has led to a spurt in the demand for diesel. According to officials of the state level coordination office of oil companies, the shortage was temporary and fresh stocks have been sought.

Heading: Ahmedabad bandh: protestors clash with ashram supporters - Indian Express
Content:
As the ire against fishermen from Tamil Nadu coming under fire from the Lankan navy mounted in the state, the Centre is reportedly considering giving licenses to local fishermen to fish in the Katchatheevu area.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has assured that he would take up the issue with Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapakse during the SAARC summit in Colombo in August, Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) president G K Mani told The Indian Express.

"Though Indian fishermen have been fishing in the area for several decades, they are now under attack from the Sri Lankan Navy, even in areas that come in Indian territorial waters. We apprised the Prime Minister about the situation and urged his interference to stop this continuous attack on our people," Mani said.

He added that the delegation of elected members of the PMK, a UPA member, were assured that the Centre would look at options like issuing licenses.

The DMK, meanwhile, will field its A-list leaders including Rajya Sabha member Kanimozhi and State Minister M K Stalin to organise a one-day fast in the coastal districts on Saturday. The high-level policy implementation committee of the DMK that met here on Thursday decided to organise the fast to "bring the situation to the urgent notice of the Government of India." Protest fasts will be held in all coastal towns, villages and district headquarters of the state.

According to a statement issued after the meeting, the party was concerned at the indiscriminate firing on fishermen from the state by the Sri Lankan Navy, the most recent incidents being reported on July 2 and July 12.

In the attack, adds the DMK statement, several fishermen were killed, 900 were arrested and about 300 boats were seized, generating "fear in the minds of the fishing community".

The committee has also demanded that the Centre summon the High Commissioner of Sri Lanka to express its displeasure "in strong and unequivocal terms, condemning the killing of innocent fishermen by the Sri Lankan Navy," and added that the patrolling by the Indian Navy and Coast Guard should be intensified along the IMBL so that "incursions by the Lankan Navy are prevented".

The Lankan Navy, on the other hand, has denied being involved in the shooting on these days and insisted that LTTE cadres were responsible.

Protesting these attacks, the fishing community across the state had gone on strike and refused to venture into the sea. After a meeting with the chief minister on Thursday, the representatives of the community have agreed to withdraw the strike.

Fishermen from Tamil Nadu coming under fire from the Sri Lankan Navy have always generated considerable angst in the state. After the recent incidents, the State Government and the ruling party had been criticised by the Opposition for its failure to prevent the attacks despite sharing power at both the Centre and the state.

PMK founder S Ramadoss ridiculed the protest fast organised by the DMK as a 'drama'. Giving up rights over the Katchatheevu area to Sri Lanka in 1974 was the primary reason for the present situation where over 800 Tamil fishermen have lost their lives due to the attack by the armed forces of the island country, he said.

Ramadoss has demanded that this agreement between India and Sri Lanka should be scrapped.

Heading: Relax quality curbs to fill officers’ posts: MoD - Indian Express
Content:
Violence and attacks on journalists and locals by supporters of spiritual leader Asaram Bapu on Friday marred a bandh called by residents to protest against the death of two boys of an ashram run by him here.

The police opened fire and lobbed dozens of teargas shells to control arson after devotees of the Asaram Bapu Ashram — wielding lathis, swords and pistols — attacked protestors in Ahmedabad. The devotees also demanded a fair probe into the mysterious death of the boys, whose bodies were found on the banks of the Sabarmati river more than two weeks ago.

The Ahmedabad bandh coincided with Guru Poornima celebrations organised by the ashram. Several people, including mediapersons covering the celebrations in Motera village and those on a protest march near the ashram, were attacked by devotees. Strangely, the ashram did not tell its marauding devotees to stop indulging in violence.

The police, who initially chose not to intervene while the armed followers went beserk, later fired shots in the air and lobbed more than three-dozen tear gas shells when protestors decided to take on the attackers.

Angry locals soon spread over the Sabarmati area and other locations in the city, pelting stones and setting fire to vehicles, thus mounting retaliatory attacks. About 40 cars and many other vehicles were burnt by the protestors.

The mayhem began at 11 a m when a mob of nearly 2,000 followers from the ashram got out and began attacking locals gathered outside in protest. The mob threw stones at the gathering, injuring several people, including Gandhinagar Superintendent of Police Piyush Patel.

On being attacked, the protestors tried to flee, but were pursued by the followers who went after them with lathis. The followers also broke into nearby housing societies, ransacking and damaging property. The violence ended after more than half-an-hour.

"The ashram inmates just barged in and damaged at least 20 vehicles parked in our society complex," said Rajesh Kumar, a resident of Stadium Villa Bungalows here. Soon, locals teamed up to target the followers, who were on their way to participate in the Guru Poornima celebrations.

Ahmedabad Joint Commissioner of Police Mohan Jha refused to comment on the role of the police. DIG J K Bhatt claimed that the situation was under control. The police, he claimed, "have arrested 10 to 15 people." However, ashram administrator Uday Sangani was unavailable for comments.

Friday's violence was a fallout of the death of two schoolchildren — Dipesh Vaghela and Abhishek Vaghela — whose bodies were recovered on July 5 after they went missing from the ashram-run gurukul on July 3. Their parents alleged that the two were used for sorcery rites and done to death. The internal organs of one of the boys were missing, and both ears missing in the other, said family members.

Heading: Cabinet clears life term for dealing in spurious drugs - Indian Express
Content:
In a move that is bound to create controversy, the Defence Ministry has recommended a one-time relaxation in quality requirements of selection boards to fill crucial gaps in the officer cadre of the armed forces.

With a shortage of more than 12,000 officers in the Army alone, the ministry has written to the three services with the suggestion as an extraordinary measure to mitigate the situation.

While the suggestion was sent after an expert panel put forward its views to Defence Minister A K Antony earlier this year, opinion on the matter is divided with the Armed Forces contending that any dilution in standards would lead to serious leadership problems.

Several serving and retired officers have come out strongly against the idea by saying that other measures, including better pay benefits, are required to recruit and retain talent in the armed forces.

"Any dilution of quality standards will inevitably lead to poor leadership at the junior level and is best avoided. Other innovative measures are needed to attract and retain the best talent in the country for the armed forces," said Brigadier Gurmeet Kanwal (retd), Director, Centre for Land Warfare Studies (CLAWS).

The rejection rate of Service Selection Boards being over 95 per cent, sources say that the ministry has made these suggestions after persistent projections of shortages by the Armed Forces.

The MoD has also suggested tightening the grant of Premature Retirement (PMR) to officers to mitigate the shortage. Noting that a large number of officers are being granted an early release from service, the ministry has suggested that guidelines under which PMR is granted need to be revised at the earliest.

Heading: Ten skip party meet, but SP puts up brave face - Indian Express
Content:
Manufacturing and selling spurious drugs could now mean a lifetime behind bars. In a bid to tighten the noose around those involved in the illegal business, the Union Cabinet on Thursday approved amendments to the Drugs and Cosmetics (Amendment) Bill 2005 that has provisions for harsher punishments.

Many offences under the Act that were earlier bailable and non-cognisable, have now become non-bailable and cognisable. And the new penalties include imprisonment for a term that shall not be less than 10 years and may extend to life, and fine imposed shall not be less than Rs 10 lakh or thrice the value of drugs confiscated, whichever is more.

Earlier, those convicted under the Act had to spend a maximum of five years in jail and pay a fine of not more than Rs 10,000.

The Health Ministry estimates that five per cent of drugs in India are counterfeit while 0.3 per cent are spurious. A counterfeit medicine has no active ingredient or is an expired drug that has been re-labelled and sold. A fake drug does not resemble the original at all.

Heading: CPM meet today, Somnath left out of party whip - Indian Express
Content:
While the SP Parliamentary Party on Friday issued a three-line whip to its MPs to be present in the Lok Sabha on July 21 and 22 and vote in favour of the Government, three of its MPs were set not to toe the party line. Not sure of one of its two jailed MPs, the party was banking on its effective strength of 35 — out of 39 MPs.

As the Congress camp, too, took these numbers for granted, invitations were sent to the SP MPs for the July 20 dinner being hosted by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the eve of the special session of the Lok Sabha.

At the SP meeting, however, as many as 10 MPs — Beni Prasad Verma, Raj Babbar, Atiq Ahmed, Afzal Ansari, Saleem Sherwani, Usha Verma, S Bangarappa, Jaiprakash, Rajnarain Budhaulia and Munawwar Hasan — were absent.

Party leaders played it down and claimed that only three MPs — Munawwar Hasan, Jaiprakash and Rajnarain Budhaulia — were likely to defy the party whip during the trust motion. "We do not bother about these people going away," said SP general secretary Amar Singh after the meeting.

The SP leaders said though Beni Prasad Verma and Raj Babbar were suspended from the party, they would be voting for the Government. Saleem Sherwani and Usha Verma could not attend the meeting due to personal reasons. While Atiq Ahmed and Afzal Ansari were in jail, S Bangarappa was on his way but could not make it to the meet, they added.

During the meeting, party chief Mulayam Singh explained the reason for SP's support to the Congress-led Government. He is learnt to have termed Mayawati's aggression against his party as one of the crucial reasons for closing ranks with the Congress. He also told the MPs that the deal was in the national interest.

Apart from Mulayam, SP leaders Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav, who were briefed by the National Security Advisor on the nuclear deal on July 2, informed the MPs about the reasons behind supporting the deal. They are learnt to have assured the MPs that the support to the Government was in the party's interest as well.

Mohan Singh, the senior party MP in Lok Sabha, urged the MPs to "honour Mulayam's commitment" of supporting the Government. Ramjilal Suman, another senior MP, urged the party to continue raising the issue of inflation in Parliament as it affected the common man.

Soon after the meeting, Mulayam and Amar visited the Imam of Delhi's Jama Masjid to apprise him of his party's decision. The Imam is learnt to have told the SP leaders that the deal could not be "for or against" the Muslims of the country.

Heading: Poaching of MPs picks pace - Indian Express
Content:
With Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee refusing to relent, the CPI(M) on Friday appeared to have given up hope on his resigning before the July 22 trust vote, though it has become clear that his defiance will be hotly debated at the party's Central Committee meeting here this weekend.

The party has issued a three-line whip to all its MPs, asking them to be present in the House on July 21 and 22 and vote against the confidence motion, but excluded Chatterjee from the whip since he continued to occupy the Speaker's post.

The party has started thinking about the post-trust vote scenario and the main agenda of the Central Committee meeting beginning on Saturday would be to assess the preparation for the next Lok Sabha elections and the strategies to be devised in the states.

Senior leaders said the two-day meet would brainstorm on ways to cash in on the stand taken by the party on the nuclear deal issue, which it has already begun exploiting by launching a nationwide campaign, and how to hitch other issues like price rise to the nuclear bandwagon.

For the time being, the party seems to have reconciled to the prospect of Chatterjee chairing the trust vote but the Central Committee, the party's highest decision-making body, will take a hard look at the matter given the fact that general secretary Prakash Karat had said that the Speaker would take a decision "taking into account the circumstances".

The circumstances were evident as the Left had withdrawn support to the Government and Karat had given a call to defeat the ruling coalition at any cost and the logical decision in line with the party position would have been to resign from the Speakership and vote against the Government, a CPI(M) leader said.

Since Chatterjee, an MP elected on a CPI(M) ticket, had not taken this decision, it would be taken note of. But it was unlikely that the 86-member Central Committee would press him to resign and, in all probability, would only reiterate Karat's statement that it was up to the Speaker to take a decision, CPI(M) sources said. But if an overwhelming majority of the members feel that something more should be done, the situation would become different. The options available before the party are: to publicly disassociate itself from the activities of the veteran Communist and direct the West Bengal state committee to take disciplinary action against him.

The party appears to be divided on the question of what the Speaker should or should not do, with one section believing that he had indeed breached discipline. They are of the view that if he does not resign even after the trust vote, disciplinary action ought to be initiated against him.

Chatterjee had abdicated his Central Committee membership when he became the Speaker.

Heading: Menon briefs NSG members, IAEA Board on safeguards agreement - Indian Express
Content:
With D-Day inching closer, both NDA and UPA are trying their best to poach 'vulnerable' MPs.

While the UPA is trying to woo at least two JD(U) MPs, rival NDA has set its eyes on five RJD MPs from Bihar.

NDA sources in Bihar on Friday confirmed that three JD(U) MPs — one each from Bihar, Lakshadweep and UP — look vulnerable and in a bid to pay back the party leadership was considering to win over at least five RJD MPs.

"Several RJD MPs have been in touch with us for long. Since UPA began targeting our MPs, we are also considering poaching in their territory. A decision in this regard would be taken soon," a top JD(U) leader told The Indian Express.

While JD(U) MPs — one each of Lakshadweep and UP— were ready to cross over due to regional compulsions, the one from Bihar is reportedly interested as Chief Minister Nitish Kumar is unlikely to field him in the next Lok Sabha elections.

Similarly, the RJD MPs are eager to join the JD(U) in Bihar not only because of delimitation of their constituencies but also because there are clear signals from the leadership that they will not be given tickets this time.

The JD(U) had been averse in accepting them, as the leadership felt that they might become "liabilities" to the party.

In the changed circumstances, however, a JD(U) leader now said, "We are in touch with the RJD MPs and will soon decide on accepting them."

At the meeting of NDA chief ministers on Thursday, Kumar and Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi had strongly favoured that they roll out a plan to topple the UPA Government.

In this regard, Kumar had even held talks with JMM chief Shibu Soren recently, offering to make him Jharkhand Chief Minister, said party sources.

Heading: Manipur MP wants Cong, BJP to clear stand on Greater Nagaland - Indian Express
Content:
Lobbying for the Indo-US nuclear deal, India on Friday briefed the IAEA Board of Governors and some NSG countries on the safeguards agreement amid reports that there was no sign of opposition to the accord.

After discussing the text of the India-specific safeguards accord with International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief Mohamed ElBaradei, Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon told representatives of the 54 countries that the text was a good one. Among the 35 members of the IAEA Board of Governors, 26 are also part of Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).

The remaining 19 NSG countries were also invited for the special briefing held at a venue outside the premises of the IAEA secretariat in the run-up to the IAEA Board's scheduled meeting in Vienna on August 1. Approval of the India-specific safeguards agreement by the IAEA Board is an important step in the operationalisation of the n-deal.

The briefing significantly coincided with the third anniversary of the July 18, 2005 India-US civil nuclear understanding. Menon is understood to have allayed apprehensions about the fallout of the pact on the nuclear non-proliferation regime.

At the briefing, Menon is understood to have highlighted the importance of the Indo-US nuclear deal initiative while citing the country's impeccable track record on non-proliferation front despite not being a signatory to NPT.

ElBaradei, a strong advocate of the deal, also met US Under Secretary of State William Burns for talks on the nuke accord. Burns, the third ranking US diplomat, was despatched by the Bush administration for "consultations" on the nuke pact in an attempt to push the deal.

Heading: Meghalaya: experts to study impact of uranium mining - Indian Express
Content:
Independent Lok Sabha MP from Outer Manipur Mani Charanamei on Friday said he would decide on whom to support during the July 22 trust vote only after both the Congress and the BJP make their stand on the Greater Nagaland issue clear.

Talking over phone from New Delhi on Friday, Charanamei told The Indian Express that both the parties have been lobbying with him for his vote. He, however, said: "I have not decided whether to oppose or support the trust vote as the Nagas also have their own issue of unification of Naga-inhabited areas with Nagaland." However, Charanamei's disappointment with the Centre was obvious when he said that the UPA Government's Common Minimum Programme had explicitly said that the "territorial boundary" of the northeast would be maintained, saying this "tries to subdue the Naga aspiration".

Heading: ‘Save Majuli’ campaign finds new patron in Assam Governor - Indian Express
Content:
During its first meeting on Friday, the all-party committee constituted by the Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) coalition Government on uranium mining decided to form three groups of experts to study the implications of uranium mining by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) in Kylleng-Pyndeng-Sohiong in West Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya.

CM Donkupar Roy, the chairman of the committee, said while one expert group would be from outside the state, the other two would comprise officials from Meghalaya. One of these groups will include officials from the state health department, who will visit Domasiat, known for its uranium reserves, where some locals were involved in looking for the radioactive element with an official of the Atomic Mineral Division (AMD) in 1991.

However, some members of the committee verbalised their misgivings, most notably Deputy Chief Minister and Hill State People's Democratic Party (HSPDP) president H S Lyngdoh and Urban Affairs Minister and Khyun Hynniwtrep National Awakening Movement (KHNAM) president Paul Lyngdoh.

Even as the CM was briefing the media, H S Lyngdoh interjected and said, "there are no experts who will tell us about the radiation." Paul Lyngdoh, meanwhile, rubbished the claims of UCIL's white paper that stated most people support the mining of uranium. He quoted the Deputy Commissioner's report saying "only 23 per cent" were in favour of it. He did add that his party would change its stand if the experts provided evidence that mining would not cause health hazards.

Heading: In trust vote heat, cracks appear in NCP-BJP ‘Pune Pattern’ - Indian Express
Content:
The campaign to save Majuli — the world's largest inhabited river island — received a major boost on Friday with Assam's newly appointed governor Shiv Charan Mathur joining the bandwagon and vowing to put in his best efforts to protect it.

"It is my priority not just to help save this historically and culturally important island from Brahmaputra's fury, but also to help get the World Heritage Site tag for it," said Mathur, who was here on a day-long visit, during an interaction with the islanders.

The Governor also promised to meet the Prime Minister in August to exclusively discuss the issue of saving Majuli. "I promise to see the Prime Minister next month and discuss with him the problems faced by this wonderful island," he said. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh incidentally has already disappointed the islanders by failing to keep his date with the island thrice in the past four years.

The area of Majuli has come down from about 1,260 sq km to just about 600 sq km over a period of seven decades with the Brahmaputra causing severe bank erosion almost every year.

"The fate of Majuli should be also considered a matter of national concern. Majuli does not belong just to the people of Assam. It should be called India's treasure island," he said. It was in Majuli that Sankaradeva, the 16th century Vaishnavite saint, had launched his socio-religious reforms movement that continues to bind Assamese society.

Heading: NO LESSON IN TOLERANCE - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when affiliations are getting a re-look, the aftershocks are being felt in Pune where a unique arrangement has held fast over the past one year.

Dubbed the Pune Pattern, it saw the coming together of Sharad Pawar's NCP, the BJP and Shiv Sena to keep the Congress out of power in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC). It was in keeping with the NCP's politics in the state, which has seen it taking liberties with its ally (and rival), the Congress, since the last Assembly polls in 2004.

However, the situation in Delhi has perhaps prompted allies in the ruling coalition as well as in the Opposition to bare their "true" alignments. Last week, during the campaign for Legislative Council polls from the Pune graduates' constituency, the fissures came forth.

BJP's Gopinath Munde accused NCP chief Sharad Pawar and the latter's nephew and state minister Ajit Pawar of land-grabbing, and the Pawars retaliated with asking him to find some new allegations. Pawar Senior added that he did not own any land outside Baramati.

Workers of both the parties took to the streets in Pune, Mumbai, Thane and several parts of the state, burning effigies and attacking their opponents. While the Pune Pattern now hangs by a thread, plans for similar alignments in other local bodies may be shelved too.

Before the Pune arrangement, in 2006, the NCP had teamed up with the Sena and the BJP to see Rahul Bajaj enter the Rajya Sabha, defeating the Congress's Avinash Pande. Again, during the recent Sangli Municipal Corporation elections, the three had come together. However, with elections a certainty, it appears that the parties want to show that their "arrangements" were local and will have no effect on their national alignments. For the NCP, especially, it is important to show itself as one of the most loyal allies of the Congress. The reason being that in Maharashtra, the Pune Pattern has hurt Congress leaders. The outgoing Maharashtra PCC chief Prabha Rau, who was appointed Governor of Himachal Pradesh recently, has been openly saying that her party workers are against a pre-poll alliance with the NCP and that her party would never forget the Pune arrangement.

The flexing of muscle by Munde and Ajit Pawar, who is considered the architect of the Pune Pattern, is also not surprising. Pune apart, Munde has been a staunch critic of the Pawars and his strong campaign against Pawar, when he was the CM, is believed to have been one of the factors behind the victory of Sena-BJP against the Congress government in 1995.

With both Munde and Ajit Pawar seen as future chief ministers by their supporters, the vehement reaction to their clash was but expected.

The political scenario in the state has also changed since the 2004 polls, which saw the NCP emerge as the single-largest party with 71 MLAs in the House of 288, followed by the Congress with 69. The "secular" parties had formed a coalition government, headed by Vilasrao Deshmukh.

Since then, Shiv Sena leader Narayan Rane has joined the Congress (2005), and engineered the crossover of seven more Sena MLAs, six of whom got re-elected on Congress tickets. This has taken the Congress tally to 75 and made it the single-largest party in the House. Besides, there are players like the BSP and Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) in the picture now.

The Sena, which is finding its feet after being shattered by the exit of Raj and Rane, and the BJP (which is witnessing growing factionalism — the most glaring being the Munde resignation episode) perhaps feel the need to consolidate their position in their traditional votebanks. In such a scenario, the ambitious Pune Pattern is hardly likely to be replicated in the state.

Heading: Badlands now site of salvation - Indian Express
Content:
The Kerala Government on Thursday decided to remove certain controversial portions from class VII social science textbook in a bid to end the raging textbook controversy in the state. Simultaneously, the state Government also ruled out withdrawal of the textbook, a demand made by the Congress-led Opposition. This political and religious debate is only the latest addition to an eventful history of textbook controversies that have plagued the country time and again. Here's a look at some recent ones:

•JUNE 2008: Religious leaders and the opposition parties in Kerala go up in arms and the state witnesses widespread agitations over the contents of a chapter entitled Life without religion in class VII social science book. The ruling LDF is accused of attempting to spread communism and atheism among the students.

•JUNE 2008: The Goa Government withdraws two NCERT textbooks — History and Hindi — after objections raised by anti-tobacco groups and NGOs over numerous factual errors in the textbooks, in addition to the picture of a French commander smoking.

•JUNE 2008: In its efforts to modify academic curriculum, as part of the National Curriculum Framework, the NCERT replaces a class VIII book on the biography of Gautam Buddha written by Ashvaghosh, Buddhacharita, with Jawaharlal Nehru's Bharat Ek Khoj. Buddhist and SC/ST organisations consider this a sign of disrespect and an attempt to moot the "Nehru/Gandhi-centric vision", to replace "literature" with "history".

•MARCH 2008: The BJP raises hue and cry over the essay, Three Hundred Ramayanas: Five Examples and Three Thoughts on Translation, by A K Ramanujan as part of the Delhi university's Bachelor of Arts (BA) programme and considers it "an attempt to denigrate the Ramayana and create serious doubts about the existence of Ram, Sita and Laxman".

•2007: Protests in Uttar Pradesh over controversial content regarding sex education. The state Government withdraws the book from curriculum.

•2006: NCERT's decision to introduce topics such as the 2002 Gujarat riots, the Ayodhya dispute and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in class XII political science textbook is seen as an attempt by the UPA Government to propagate the "Congress' agenda", and portraying the Narendra Modi government in a bad light.

•2006: The BJP is severely critical of the textbook, Modern Indian History, by Bipin Chandra, reintroduced by the NCERT, which describes Jats as lutera or looters, and Lokmanya Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh and Bipin Chandra Pal as terrorists.

•2004: The newly elected UPA Government's efforts to modify NCERT textbooks for classes VI and VII is seen by the BJP as an attempt to "distort" history and especially to give a "false account' of Sikhism.

•2004: Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi alleges that the deletion of the word "Gujarat" from the national anthem printed in the class IX textbook by the Kerala Education Department was a deliberate "mischief".

•2004: Controversy erupts in Gujarat over the glorification of Nazism and the Holocaust in social studies textbooks for classes IX and X.

•2002: NCERT is in the midst of controversies after its class XII history textbook does not mention the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi in 1948, and there's an "exaggerated" reference to Vedic civilisation.

Heading: A saga of bloopers - Indian Express
Content:
Thanks to an image makeover, improved infrastructure and a state government keen on selling itself to the international market, Bihar is fast becoming a favoured tourist destination among foreigners. Considered the badlands by some, the state has witnessed an unprecedented surge in foreign tourists — mainly Buddhists hailing from neighbouring Sri Lanka to Japan, South Korea, North Korea and European countries — over the last three to four years.

Between January and June this year, the number of foreign tourists visiting the area has crossed the one lakh mark, and it is expected to exceed 2.5 lakh by year's end. 

The number of foreign tourists jumped from 63,321 in 2005 to 94,446 in 2006 to 1,77,301 in 2007.

The state experiences peak foreign tourists inflow during December and January. In fact, in January 2007, foreign tourists (55,030) outnumbered domestic tourists (35,473) at Bodhgaya. Further, Patna, Gaya, Rajgir and Raxaul saw 300, 266, 700, and 362 foreign tourists, respectively, in the same month.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Principal Tourism Secretary Rashmi Verma said, "Foreigners now consider Bihar a safe tourist destination. We have created more national and international awareness regarding our rich cultural heritage."

Verma added that the state's representatives took part in various prestigious international tourism marts in Berlin and London last year.

Verma said that when the "triangle road" between Patna, Bodhgaya and Rajgir is widened in two to three years' time, more number of foreign tourists are likely to venture to the other locales as well. In order to capitalise on foreign interest, the state Government has earmarked large sums for improvements throughout the region.

Bodhygaya receives the most number of foreign tourists because of its international airport and good accommodations.

Tourist spots on the popular Buddhist and Hindu pilgrimage circuits include Golghar and Kumhrar in Patna; the Bodhi tree, Mahabodhi Temple, Vajrasan and Vishnupad Temple in Bodhgaya; the ropeway, Venuvan, hot water springs and Jarasandh ka akhara in Rajgir; Nalanda University and Nalanda Museum; Biharsharif; Vishwa Shanti Stupa and Ashokan Temple in Vaishali.Foreign tourists in Bihar
