And it isn't just runs, the strange mode of dismissals or the minutes' section on the scorecard that was responsible for the relaxed mood in the Indian camp. More importantly, it is the composition of this tour party that gives a comforting feel to the players, especially to the batting line-up.

It's been a long time since such a settled batting line-up has been put together. With all the batters picking themselves for the Test to start on Wednesday, that uncomfortable feeling of a sword hanging on their heads is a welcome change. With 21-year-old Rohit Sharma as the only back-up batsman in the squad, the seniors this time around don't have to repeatedly look behind their backs. As things stand, Sharma seems more like an option that can only be tried in case of an injury and not because of someone's temporary loss of form.

In case there was someone like Yuvraj Singh, or say even a Mohammad Kaif, on the bench, things would have been different. Speculation about the Test playing XI would have kicked off the moment the ball hit Laxman's stumps or when Ganguly was out miscuing the pull. Statistics such as the number of games Yuvraj or Kaif have spent on the sidelines were likely to be quoted, and stories of a senior vs junior slant would have been churned out from Colombo.

It can be argued that complacency can creep in with a few options in the dressing room; but if, for once, the batsmen, who have been under constant scrutiny, find themselves in a comfort zone, it's an experiment worth pursuing. Opener Gautam Gambhir might have been out cheaply in the game, but coach Gary Kirsten has given enough indications that he is here to find long-term solutions and that means he would prefer specialists.

There's only one way in which the present batting line-up can be disturbed and that is if the team management opts for five bowlers. Traditionally, in the first Test of a series, India rarely go with a batsman short and that happens to be the thought process in the dressing room too.

So, as the Indians walked towards the team bus, there were several smiles on the faces despite the reading on the scoreboard. Tongues can wag because of a bad day at the office, but to counter that, all they need to do is shut their ears and focus on the Test ahead. This time around there are no edgy fingers hovering around the panic button.

Heading: If you lose trust vote, don’t try to push deal, Karat warns Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Sena MPs: Rane, Deshmukh on job - Indian Express
Content:
Having cobbled together an alliance of disparate parties to lead Operation Topple, the CPM on Sunday claimed that both the Indo-US nuclear deal and the Government would be "doomed" on July 22 and warned the UPA against trying to push the agreement in the event of losing the trust vote.

On the day the UNPA, Left parties and the BSP came together on a common platform with a "single agenda to bring down the Government", CPM general secretary Prakash Karat threw broad hints that the arrangement was going to stay even after the trust vote, in first signs that a third alternative could take shape.

"The Central Committee asked us to gather more such forces to ensure that there will be a way forward after the trust vote," Karat said after the two-day meeting of the party's Central Committee.

"More such forces are joining us. There will be a way forward after the trust vote... More and more forces are coming together to fight the Government," he said, noting that the UNPA, BSP, JD(S), RLD and the Left have decided to work together.

The Central Committee, the highest decision-making body of the party in between two party Congress meets, endorsed the Politburo decision to withdraw support to the Government because of the "undemocratic" and "totally uncalled for" decision to go ahead with the nuclear deal.

"The deal will be doomed and the Government will be doomed on July 22," Karat said as he sharpened his attack on the Congress-led Government for resorting to "desperate and unscrupulous efforts to engineer defections and win over unaffiliated members of Parliament."

"We wish to warn this Government that in case you lose the trust vote, don't try and push the nuclear deal. The country will revolt," he said, alleging that the Government had already bypassed Parliament and gone back on its public pledge to implement a commitment given to US President George W Bush.

Charging the Government with "public betrayal", he said it had promised the next step on the safeguards agreement would be taken only after the trust vote. Instead, "we see the spectacle of our officers scurrying to Vienna to try and hustle through the safeguards agreement with the (IAEA) Board of Governors."

"It is shocking that the Manmohan Singh Government went to the (IAEA) Board of Governors for approval of the draft safeguards agreement without revealing the text to the country. The 123 Agreement with the US was similarly signed without taking the country into confidence. The most recent betrayal by the Government has been the going back on its public commitment not to approach the Board of Governors without facing the trust motion in Lok Sabha," he said.

Karat was scathing in his criticism of the Samajwadi Party, now in the UPA camp, accusing it of trying to mobilise the support of unaffiliated MPs using "money power and unscrupulous methods".

He said the SP had betrayed the Left twice earlier. "This is not the first time that the SP is doing so. It has betrayed the country and others twice earlier in 1999 and in 2002. This is the third time," he said.

In 1999, the BJP-led government was brought down and "all secular parties wanted to bring a secular government" but the SP backed out at the last minute, enabling the return of the BJP and its allies. Again in 2002, the SP walked out of the People's Front, of which veteran Marxist Jyoti Basu was the president and Mulayam Singh Yadav the convenor. The issue was supporting K R Narayanan as the Presidential nominee.

"The SP walked out of the Front at the last moment and supported the NDA representative (A P J Abdul Kalam). And now it is the nuclear deal," Karat said. "We had not asked the SP to oppose the nuclear deal. But their leaders campaigned against it inside and outside Parliament. The speeches of their leaders (opposing the deal) are part of Parliamentary records. But today the SP, at the instance of the Congress, is supporting the United States as well as the deal," he said.

Heading: Prayers for Manmohan - Indian Express
Content:
With the UPA Government at the Centre facing a crucial trust vote on Tuesday, speculations about the Congress wooing away some Shiv Sena MPs have gained momentum.

It is believed that Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Revenue Minister Narayan Rane are in touch with some disgruntled MPs from the Sena to help UPA gather the numbers ahead of the vote. Deshmukh also left for New Delhi on Sunday.

As the Sena MPs met in party chief Bal Thackeray's Bandra residence on Saturday to affirm their support to NDA, MP Tukaram Renge-Patil from Parbhani in Marathwada was absent. Sixty-year-old Patil, a resident of Jamb in Parbhani, is a first term MP, and is still said to be untraceable. He is reportedly not on good terms with local Sena functionaries including Parbhani MLA Sanjay Jadhav and is hence insecure about being re-nominated from the party.

Sena MP Kalpana Narhire from Osmanabad who is unsure of her political future with her constituency — a reserved one — being opened up during the recent delimitation exercise is also under scrutiny. There are reports that the Congress is also eyeing Sena MPs from Vidarbha and Konkan to bolster its numbers ahead of the crucial trust vote.

Admitting that Patil was not present at the party's meeting in New Delhi on Sunday, Sena Rajya Sabha MP and Saamana executive editor Sanjay Raut said they were hopeful that he would make it to the trust vote. Adding that Patil's phone was not reachable, Raut said his family had told them that he would make it to New Delhi. "He has been our long-time activist for almost 25 years and a two-term MLA and now an MP. We do not want to doubt him," added Raut, while trying to dismiss reports that Rane was trying to woo Sena MPs.

"As long as he does not present himself, what can we say?" said Raut, while responding to questions about speculations that Deshmukh, who also hails from Marathwada, may have influenced Patil to join ranks with the Congress.

Rane supporters meanwhile said the Revenue Minister, who has scores to settle with his former party, was keeping his cards close to his chest, but said there were chances that he may engineer defections from the Sena. Rane, who was in Kankavali on Sunday, before leaving for Mumbai, had visited New Delhi recently for a meeting with the Congress top brass, fuelling speculations.

Heading: Rainfall in peninsular India may improve by July-end - Indian Express
Content: As the countdown began for the make or break trust vote, prayers were held at several places in Punjab on Sunday for continuation of the UPA Government led by Manmohan Singh, country's first Sikh Prime Minister. "Akhand Paath" (non-stop recital of Sikhs' holy book Guru Granth Sahib) and "Ardas" (prayers) were held in Chandigarh, Jalandhar, Amritsar and other places for survival of the Government. "Various Sikh bodies have been praying for Singh. The family too has been praying for the continuation of the Government to enable Singh to serve the nation further," Surjit Singh Kohli, younger brother of the Prime Minister said.

Heading: Asaram ashram apologises for attack on mediapersons, calls it unfortunate - Indian Express
Content:
The July rainfall has practically disappointed farmers in the southern peninsula, Gujarat, Maharashtra and parts of northeastern India. The official weather forecasting agency, India Meteorological Department (IMD), has not extended any immediate hope for the revival of the situation. Its numerical weather prediction models have said "subdued rainfall activity would continue over central and western India in the next three to four days".

The US-based Center for Ocean Land Atmosphere Administration (COLA) in its short-term forecast for the period till July 26 has also confirmed low rainfall of 20 to 35 mm in western and parts of central and southern India. It, however, predicted heavy rainfall of over 150 mm in the heartland of north India, eastern and northeastern India, Andhra Pradesh and parts of central India.

According to COLA, the situation is likely to improve after July 27, when most parts of the country would receive good showers.

The other US-based agencies like Climate Prediction Center, National Centers for Environmental Prediction and weather service of National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) have noted the transition from La Nina to neutral conditions in the central and east-central equitorial Pacific during June. La Nina or cooling of Pacific waters below normal is usually responsible for good rains and the country enjoyed good rains in June, this year.

However, the possibility of emergence of the spoilsport, El Nino (warming of Pacific waters) is ruled out. This dispels the apprehensions of a severe drought year to an extent.

Weather conditions also depend upon the surrounding sea surface temperatures (SSTs). The International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRICS) predicted "a weak positive dipole" in the equatorial Indian Ocean with slightly below average SSTs near Indonesia and slightly above average SSTs near the African coast.

July rainfall is crucial for Indian agriculture in the four-month S-W Monsoon season. The IMD has predicted the country will receive rainfall amounting to 98% of its long period average of 293 mm on cumulative basis in July, subject to a model error of +/-9%. Till the middle of the month the cumulative rainfall has been 321.8 mm which is 4% more than the normal. But Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh and parts of northeastern India did not receive good rainfall and as a result sowing operations were badly affected in these areas.

Sowing operations for groundnut, red gram, black gram, green gram, cotton, sugarcane and millets like jowar were affected.

The July Fallout

•13 out of 36 meteorological subdivisions received deficient rains

•Marathwada worst hit

•35% of meteorological districts received deficient to scanty rains

•Peninsular India gets 34% less rains

•Rainfall deficient over central India by 3%

•Areas under groundnut, red gram, black gram, green gram, cotton, sugarcane and jowar shrink

•Hope hinges on good rainfall distribution by month-end

Heading: Gujarat bandh today - Indian Express
Content:
Admitting that followers of Asaram Bapu were involved in the Friday's attack on the locals and journalists in Motera, ashram authorities on Sunday apologised for the incident on Sunday.

Ashram administrator Uday Sangani said the followers resorted to violence in self-defence. "We had got reports that the followers of Asaram Bapu, who were on their way to attend the Guru Purnima celebrations at the ashram, were being waylaid and harassed by the locals. Their vehicles too were damaged," he said.

"The ashram inmates lost their calm and retaliated. It is unfortunate that the mediapersons, too, had to bear the brunt. We are sorry for that."

Sangani denied having any information about Asaram Bapu's alleged address to the sadhaks to launch the attack.

Meanwhile, Asaram Bapu, in full-page advertisements in vernaculars on Sunday, distanced his ashram from the controversy surrounding the death of two of his Gurukul boys.

He said the entire rampage episode was a well-planned conspiracy.

"Dipesh and Abhishek drowned to death. They had apparently gone to play in the riverbed. The Gurukul neither believes in nor conducts black magic. The boys died in an accident and were not sacrificed for any ritual."

He, however, said that the ashram was ready to pay compensation to the mediapersons who were attacked.

Asaram, in the advertisements, has quoted Ram Charit Manas and renowned religious and spiritual figures to send his message across.

"Asaramji is a ray of hope for every blessed person," Yoga guru Baba Ramdev has been quoted as saying.

"Bapu is always new, always growing and a sacred soul," Kathakar Morari Bapu has been quoted in the advertisements.

Bodies of Dipesh and Abhishek were recovered from the Sabarmati riverbed on July 5.

Heading: MTNL ad sees humour in BMC’s monsoon worries - Indian Express
Content:
An amalgamation of 15 social organisations, led by Jagega Gujarat Sangharash Samiti (JGSS), has called for Gujarat bandh on Monday to protest against the mysterious death of two students of the Asaram Gurukul.

"We expect people from across Gujarat to voluntarily support the bandh and register their protest against the gruesome incident and the state Government's inertia on the issue," said JGSS convener Naresh Shah.

Earlier on Sunday, the JGSS called off its rally, from Sabarmati Ashram to Asaram Gurukul, to avoid any untoward incident. "The decision has been changed to register public protest," said Shah.

The Gujarat unit of the Congress has declared to extend support to the bandh. It will also protest against the state Government for not handing over the case to the CBI.

"It's been over 15 days, but the demand for CBI inquiry has got no response from the Government," said GPCC president Siddharath Patel.

Heading: Fraud case: SC to hear Praful plea today - Indian Express
Content:
Despite the continuing dry spell and elected representatives' demand for the state to be declared drought-prone, flooding in Mumbai continues to be in news. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), facing flak over its handling of the flooding, has so far tried to reason with suffering Mumbaiites by offering various examples about other countries and blaming global warming, but an advertisement by a government agency looks like an attempt to turn the civic body's annual discomfiture into a laughing matter.

The advertisement in question, by government-owned telephone service provider Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL), has been in print over the last few days. "Tez barsaat ka hona aam baat hai, puri Mumbai ka kaam par jaana khaas baat hai," the MTNL ad says with the backdrop of a harrowed Mumbaiite who has made his way through knee-deep flood water and neck-to-neck traffic on city roads.

Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak said he had neither seen the ad nor wished to. "We do not care about any criticism and we are not concerned if someone is taking pot-shots at us," he said. When the details of the ad were given, Phatak retorted that even BMC can issue an ad about MTNL. "Even we can say how MTNL services fail during monsoon but BMC's broom keeps doing its job. We agree there are crises but Mumbai is the most sought after city and people continue to come here. If there is a lull then the market will show," he said. "We are busy ensuring the city moves on and are interested in maintaining the machinery."

The MTNL on its part had said they wanted to show how Mumbaiites find their way through difficulties — read flood — during monsoon. "We did not intend to take any pot shots. The advertising is humorous in its intention and showed that MTNL is a special phone for the citizens," said MTNL assistant general manager (Public Relations) A N Deshpande.

Heading: SC for All-India Judicial Service - Indian Express
Content:
On Monday, July 21, the Supreme Court will hear a petition filed by Civil Aviation Minister Praful Patel. The minister is seeking a direction to halt the proceedings of a Rs 50 crore fraud case involving a company he once chaired. The matter will be heard by a bench headed by Justice Ashok Bhan. Earlier, the apex court stayed the Bombay High Court's direction that the trial court proceed by seeking a CBI probe.

According to Patel, in April 2004, Unit Trust of India (UTI) filed a complaint before the magistrate's court against nine directors of Mumbai-based Auto Riders Finance Ltd alleging that the directors misappropriated the security given against a Rs 50-crore loan borrowed between 1993 and 1995 intended for setting up the auto finance company.

Patel, who was a non-executive director and chairman, learned about the complaint through newspapers, the 2006 apex court petition stated. Moreover, UTI later sought deletion of three names, including that of Patel, on the grounds that they had ceased to be directors since March 1999 and were not concerned with day-to-day workings of the company.

According to Patel, the magistrate had deleted his name and the names of T N V Ayyar and Surendra Ruia on November 19, 2004, and the order had not been challenged till the filing of the appeal before the apex court in 2006. However, the minister said that the High Court on August 16, 2006 had entertained two PILs filed by Delhi-based journalist M Furquan and one Shoaib, alias Richie Sequeira, and allowed the order of the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (Mumbai) that asked the petitioners to approach the High Court for a CBI probe into the scam.

The High Court asked the trial court to go ahead with seeking a CBI probe and to ignore the order passed by the magistrate in November 2004 that dropped the three accused persons and directed the complainant to move the High Court for transfer of the case to the CBI.

"The High Court ought not to have entertained a purported PIL and interfered with the proceedings before a criminal court which were proceeding as per the procedure provided under the criminal procedure," the minister said.

Heading: Only in Dharavi: residents of building to find themselves back in a slum - Indian Express
Content:
In what could be the first step towards having an All India Judicial Service, the Supreme Court has sought the views of the High Courts on the possibility of entrusting recruitment of 25 per cent posts in the higher judiciary — Additional Sessions Judges and above — to a national authority.

Sources in the Supreme Court say the national body could either be set up by the apex court in consultation with the Union Ministry of Law and Justice or the responsibility could be handed over to the Union Public Service Commission. The selection process would be on an all-India basis akin to the civil services recruitment.

Formation of an All India Judicial Service has been a long-pending demand, which has found support from members of the judiciary, jurists as well as successive governments. Sources say the proposal for having an all-India judicial service was mooted by the first, eighth and the 11th Law Commissions as well as the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice.

In at least two judgments delivered in the early '90s, even the apex court had recommended the setting up of an all-India judicial service. In fact, in its judgment in the All India Judges Association case, the SC Bench had spoken of the need for having an All-India Judicial Service.

At present, almost all states have a system of selecting members of the subordinate judiciary. But, judiciary continues to be the only service that does not boast of a national service.

Says E M Sudarsana Natchiappan, Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, "There is certainly a need to have an all-India judicial service as it would take care of the problem of shortage of judges. It would also ensure that the process of appointing judges to the higher judiciary becomes more transparent."

Heading: Don’t preach, Mulayam tells Left - Indian Express
Content:
In a city where shanty-towns proliferate almost as quickly as plans to rehabilitate the millions living in them, this will be a first. Having spent eight years in an eight-storey building in Asia's largest slum, with no toilets except on the ground floor and no electricity at all, 109 families now face "rehabilitation" in their original slum structures.

The demolition of their building in Dharavi, in Central Mumbai, was first ordered last year by the Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA), which finally found the structure to be entirely unauthorised. So, while the global big daddies of construction vie for a slice of the multi-crore Dharavi Redevelopment Project, the Anna Nagar Lokmanya Cooperative Housing Society in Dharavi faces the prospect of returning to tin-and-tarpaulin homes.

The SRA's response to the Bombay High Court after residents moved the court states: "The developer Deepak Rao of Acconor Associates carried out illegal construction work and hence the developer should demolish the unauthorised construction and should "rehabilitate" all 109 occupants by constructing their original slum structures." The developer is to bear the cost of constructing the shanties, it adds.

The residents, seeking accommodation in a transit camp instead, say it's odd that no official noticed the illegal building through these years. "We do not have even the basic amenity of a toilet on every floor. A single 1,000-litre tank supplies water to around 700 residents. And it started caving in the very year it was built," says one resident, K Anthony (37), an idli-vendor.

It was Anthony's Right to Information application that led to the discovery that their building was unauthorised. Anthony had sought details of how many flats had been sold by the developer and how many used to rehouse slum dwellers. To his shock, official records showed their SRA project had never been sanctioned.

When police complaints yielded little, residents filed a writ petition in the Bombay High Court in 2007. In reply, the SRA passed the demolition order. It emerges now that the builder started construction in 1999 despite permission being denied.

The July 2007 order, signed by then CEO of the SRA, I S Chahal, states: "The irresponsible behaviour of the developer to construct the illegal building by displacing the slumdwellers and to further argue for granting permission to the illegally constructed building is of punishable nature."

On his part, having abandoned the incomplete project, the developer Rao filed a writ petition challenging the demolition order. "We have been trying to regularise our building. The SRA, however, did not support us. In 2003, the SRA said they had misplaced our documents. How are we at fault?" Rao asks.

The SRA now awaits the court's instructions. "We will wait for the High Court to pass an order and only then will be able to shift the occupants to any transit camp," said Shrikant Singh, Chief Executive Officer of the SRA. Singh was unwilling to comment on why no action was taken against the builder.

Heading: UPA upbeat at dinner - Indian Express
Content:
With BSP supremo Mayawati trying her best to engineer defections from his party on the eve of the trust vote on July 22, SP chief Mulayam Singh Yadav on Sunday launched a broadside against the Left, charging it with playing into the BSP-BJP gambit.

Putting up a brave face in face of reports of a few party MPs toeing Mayawati's line, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said, "I want to clarify that the SP is united and those who have left us have done it for their vested interests. I consider that only one (S P Baghel) has left us. But we have also increased our tally from elsewhere." The SP paraded its MPs and later in the evening party general secretary Amar Singh claimed that BJP MP from Balrampur (UP) Brij Bhushan Singh was also with the SP in supporting the Government's trust vote.

Lashing out at the Left, Mulayam told it "not to preach secularism" to the SP. "It was the SP that weakened the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. We have reduced them to 10 seats in the state. But it is the Left parties, which are claiming themselves as more secular than us. Their true face has come out in the open," Mulayam said, adding that the Left parties were siding with the BSP chief who had even campaigned for Narendra Modi soon after Gujarat riots in 2002.

"It was Left parties that had clubbed themselves with the BJP in 1989 at the Centre, but in UP, I fought elections separately from the BJP. I had not even made a compromise when the BJP tried to demolish the Babari mosque. I have fought for secularism. Let the Left parties cite any example where they have fought the communal forces the way I have. I have not only fought against the communal forces but I have also paid the price for it. I do not make false claims like the Left," he said, ending with, "Now, Lal Krishna and Lal Jhanda (red flag) have come together."

Mulayam also came down heavily on his former colleagues in the UNPA, particularly against TDP president Chandrababu Naidu. Naidu had met Mayawati on Saturday pledging his support for her.

"Naidu sahab, you need not speak out in public. I know very well about stains on you sleeves. It is the BSP-BJP-Left along with Naidu who is roaming around and pursuing MPs not to vote for the Government. These people have taken politics to a new low. They are corrupting politics," Mulayam said even while posing a query for CPI national general secretary, "Bardhan sahab, why don't you point out who is buying MPs now. Isn't that your new colleague in the BSP. The Left has stooped so low."

Heading: M-deal better than n-deal for Ajit - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi were among the first to arrive at the Convention Hall of Ashoka Hotel, the venue of the dinner hosted by the PM ahead of the crucial trust vote.

The attraction of the party, however, was JMM chief Shibu Soren, who walked in with his flock of four MPs. In the lobby, a UPA leader was seen greeting Soren as the saviour of the Government. There were some whispers as Congress general secretary Digvijay Singh came in with Brij Bhushan Singh, a BJP MP from UP.

At the dinner, young turks like Kanimozhi and Supriya Sule shared the table with Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, while key UPA leaders Lalu Prasad Yadav, Ram Vilas Paswan and Mulayam Singh Yadav sat with the Prime Minister. Sonia preferred to remain seated at her table, while Prime Minister Singh was seen going around the hall greeting the MPs.

Despite the absentees — among them Congress MP Ambareesh — the UPA managers sounded more than confident of securing the numbers in the Lok Sabha on July 22.

Sonia's political secretary Ahmed Patel, however, appeared upbeat. "We are a thousand per cent confident. We have more than what is required," Patel told reporters. Railway Minister Lalu tried to be exuberant as always. "Mahabharat hone wala hai aur jeet hamari hogi. 292 vote milega," he declared as he emerged out of the party.

As expected RJD chief Ajit Singh, JD(S) leader Deve Gowda and some independent MPs chose to stay away.

Heading: UPA speakers get some tips - Indian Express
Content:
Whatever the fate of the Indo-US nuclear deal, the deal struck by the Rashtriya Lok Dal with the Bahujan Samaj Party on Sunday will prove to be a win-win situation for Ajit Singh.

After the talks between Ajit Singh and Mayawati, the BSP has apparently agreed to induct a Cabinet minister and two Ministers of State from the RLD in its Government. The BSP has also agreed to concede eight Lok Sabha seats to the RLD in the next General elections.

Significantly, the tie-up with BSP will help Ajit Singh send his son Jayant Singh to Parliament from the Mathura LS seat. The Congress had refused to give him the seat after its sitting MP Manvendra Singh threatened of a revolt. The RLD now has 12 MLAs in the UP Assembly and three MPs.

However, RLD state president Ram Asrey Verma refused to confirm the understanding with the BSP. "RLD has decided to join the UNPA and our three MPs will vote against the trust vote to be moved by the UPA Government on July 22," he said. "As far as the BSP deal is concerned I would be able to comment on it only after talking to my leader Ajit Singh," he added.

The party also denied that its leader has ditched the UPA Government even after it agreed to name the Amausi airport after Chowdhary Charan Singh, in lieu of support in the trust vote. "It was a proposal sent by the UP Government in 2003 to name the airport after Chowdhary Saheb, the Union Government has just implemented it now," said Verma.

The RLD's latest stand has made the Uttar Pradesh Congress jittery. "Ajit Singh bargained for a Cabinet post. He went to the BSP when the Congress refused," claimed party spokesperson Akhilesh Singh. "It is his character. In the last two decades he has been Cabinet minister in all governments at the Centre barring the present one," he added.

Heading: After call from allies, Maran says he’s with PM - Indian Express
Content: Ahead of the confidence motion, key speakers of the ruling UPA, including Rahul Gandhi, on Sunday got a briefing on the nuclear deal from National Security Advisor M K Narayanan and Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon to prepare them for the crucial debate on Monday. Gandhi will be among the speakers backing the Government in the debate on Monday.

Heading: In Kolkata, Mamata to flex muscle at rally - Indian Express
Content:
Former Union Communication Minister Dayanidhi Maran on Sunday announced that he would cast his vote in favour of the Indo-US Civilian Nuclear Deal ending days of speculations that he would abstain or even vote against the Government.

Anxious to ensure the survival of the Government, the Congress leadership and some of the alliance partners seemed to spoken to the DMK member, whom his party has not yet "bothered to contact", but for a warning to take action against any member who defied the whip. UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, Railway Minister and RJD leader Lalu Prasad, Sonia Gandhi's political advisor Ahmed Patel, State Congress leader and Union Minister G K Vasan were among those who called him, Maran said at a hurriedly called press meet at his residence on Sunday morning.

"I have decided to maintain the dignity of a DMK cadre, and I will vote in favour of the Government and support Dr Singh," said Maran, known to be close to the Congress leadership during his short but high-profile in the national capital. "I believe the deal is essential for the country. I believe the credibility of Dr Manmohan Singh, I also believe Sonia Gandhi is doing the right thing for the country," he said.

Even as his announcement came as a relief for the Government in New Delhi, he used the opportunity to vent his anger at Chief Minister M Karunanidhi's son M K Azhagiri, who has openly declared that the Maran brothers will never return to the party fold.

The speculations about his possible abstention had reasons, Maran said. "The kind of pressure put on us is well known. But even last year I voted for the candidates supported by my party. Even though I have been treated shabbily, even though people close to me are being harassed, I have decided to stand by the party," he said.

Dayanidhi, younger of the Maran brothers who own Sun TV Group, was ousted from the Union Cabinet after falling out of favour with Karunanidhi and his family. The charge was that the brothers were trying to split the first family and since their great fall, their businesses — cable TV, news and entertainment channels, and newspapers — are being targeted by the party and the State Government.

"I don't know what I did. Did I ever work against the party, or did I work against DMK candidates, did the party take any measures against me prior to this?" he asked. "Even if Karunanidhi himself wanted to reconcile, the people around him will never allow it for their personal reasons," Dayanidhi added in an open reference to Azhagiri.

However, he expressed "surprise" that the political experience of someone like Karunanidhi was not utilised to solve the present crisis that the UPA finds itself in. "I am quite surprised why the leaders in Delhi have not made use of his experience. He would have solved this crisis in a matter or minutes."

The venue had around 500 'supporters' who was raising slogans in his support, and asking him to launch a new political outfit. "I'm still in the DMK. But lets see; the future is for all to see," he said.

Heading: Tourist from Uttar Pradesh among two killed in Gulmarg blast - Indian Express
Content:
Away from the rising political temperature in Delhi, an atmosphere of political revelry has started building up in Kolkata where CPM's arch-rival, Trinamool Congress (TC), is leaving no stone unturned to make Monday's public rally at Esplanade a show of strength and its growing popularity.

Boosted by the party's spectacular performance in the recent panchayat elections and civic elections in the state, where the TC made significant inroads in CPM's strongholds, the party wants to project itself as the strongest political force to challenge Left's rule in the state.

Huge cutouts of Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee, banners and arches have come up in every part of the city leading to the rally ground. The rally is being held to mark the 15th anniversary of police firing on a Pradesh Youth Congress protest march led by Banerjee in which 13 persons were killed.

"Already 30,000 people have arrived in the city from different parts of the state. I hope at least 5 lakh people will turn up at the rally. And this will mark the beginning of the end of the CPM's misrule," Banerjee told mediapersons at her Kalighat residence on Sunday.

Eminent people from all walks of life, including West Bengal Progressive Indira Congress leader Somen Mitra, former Congress leader Atish Sinha, singer Kabir Suman, playwright Bratya Basu and human rights activist Sujata Bhadra are expected to attend the rally. "Our activists are bubbling with enthusiasm and we are working hard to make the rally a success. Thousands of our supporters have already arrived and tomorrow more will come. We have been able to defeat the CPM in villages and now we realise that the Left can be vanquished," said Ranjit Dey, a Trinamool Youth Congress leader.

Heading: Ready to run govt if people ask me: Raj to Deshmukh - Indian Express
Content:
A day after militants targeted an Army convoy on the Srinagar-Baramulla highway and killed 10 people, a grenade explosion shattered the peace in picturesque Gulmarg this afternoon, killing a tourist from Uttar Pradesh and a local resident.

With a cable car, golf course, mountain treks and a ski resort, Gulmarg is an essential tour destination in Kashmir for all seasons and Sunday's attack was clearly intended to hit the fast-reviving tourism industry in the Valley.

IGP Operations (North Kashmir) Balaji Srinivasan told The Indian Express that a grenade exploded near the ponywala stand in Gulmarg, killing Ashok Kumar, a tourist from Uttar Pradesh, and leaving several others injured. Srinivasan said at least four local residents were among the injured and had been shifted to Srinagar for treatment.

"The pony stand hardly had any tourists at that time. We feel there is some commercial interest involved in this attack," Srinivasan said. "If militants had to target tourists, then they had a better chance when there were 9,000-10,000 visitors in Gulmarg. We are investigating the case," he said.

The separatists too are questioning the motive for the attack. "We condemn any such attack. It is inhuman. But we want to know the identity of these attackers," Hurriyat leader Syed Ali Shah Geelani told The Indian Express.

Azeem Tuman, president of All Kashmir Houseboat Owners' Association, said: the attack "will certainly affect our tourism industry". He said the identity of those behind the attack should be "ascertained immediately because it harms our tourist trade".

There are fears that the attack will affect the tourism industry which had already been hit by the recent protests over the move to transfer forest land to the Amarnath Shrine board. According to the Tourism Department, around 4,51,000 tourists have already visited Kashmir this year.

Heading: Major killed in J&K gunbattle - Indian Express
Content:
After Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh's snub to Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray warning him against running a parallel government, Raj, in an open letter, written in Marathi, to Deshmukh has said he is instead interested in "running the government". The letter also calls the influx of North Indian migrants into Maharashtra a "man-made calamity," while blaming the leaders and migrants from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as being responsible for the "exploitation" of Maharashtra.

In addition, the letter alleges that MNS workers have been booked on trumped up charges by the government machinery with a political motive, and blames the influx from UP and Bihar for their "illegal dadagiri."

"You have given me and my organisation a warning about running a parallel government (but) we are interested in running the Government, and not a parallel government. In case the Maharashtrians feel so and trust us, we will do it!" said Raj, while expressing anger at Deshmukh's recent comments against the 'sons of the soil' campaigns launched by the MNS.

"No one is interested here in running a parallel government! But Chief Minister sir, as a citizen who loves Maharashtra, can't I run a small parallel party? Or, have all the constitutional rights been given out to people from UP and Bihar," added the letter.

The missive also raises issues like Marathi not being taught in English schools and corruption in licenses being given out to security agencies run by North Indians. Close on the heels of the MNS attacks on educational institutions in Pune, the letter also criticises the education barons in the state for granting admissions to students from states other than Maharashtra through underhand dealings and "shooing away Marathi students instead of granting them admissions".

Stating that it is his duty as a Maharashtrian to see whether boards on shops and establishments were in Marathi, Raj took another dig at Deshmukh, asking him to see whether the boards were in Marathi instead of trying to read and analyse "what was going on in the minds of the high command and its advisors."

Then, in a defence raised for his mode of communication, Raj wrote: "Please tell Soniaji about your opinion that writing letters is a business meant for idlers. I recently happened to read a book. Its name is Two Alone, Two Together. It has an introduction by Soniaji. It has also been edited by Sonia Gandhi. You may be surprised, but it contains letters written from 1922 to 1964 by Indira Gandhi and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru to each other. That is why I feel that Soniaji should get the kind of satisfaction that I got after listening to your theory about idlers writing letters."

Heading: Srinagar attack: ‘manual wire technique’ foiled jammers - Indian Express
Content:
Within 24 hours of a major attack on an army convoy which killed 10 armymen in the Valley, militants killed an Army Major and a head constable of the Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP) in a fierce gunbattle at Shahdra Sharief in Rajouri district on Sunday morning. Four security personnel were also injured.

Defence Ministry spokesman Lt Colonel S D Goswami identified the deceased as Major Bhanu Partap Singh of 43 Rashtriya Rifles and state police head constable Anjeev Rana of Doda. Both were killed fighting a group of heavily armed militants who were hiding in the Pangai forests adjoining Shahdra Sharief in Thana Mandi area of the district, he said, adding that the injured have been hospitalised.

The encounter started early on Sunday morning following a joint combing operation launched by security forces and the police in the area. The militants reportedly included the self-styled division commander of Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) Javed Bhai.

The lead about Javed Bhai's presence in the forests had followed the arrest of three suspected militants from Jammu railway station recently. To corner him, a team of the Special Operation Group (SOG) was specially rushed to Rajouri from Jammu. The SOG men informed the local police and security forces and later launched a joint combing operation in the area.

The exchange of fire between the two sides continued for a few hours before the militants managed to escape.

Senior Superintendent of Police, Rajouri, Rajesh Kumar said that search operations were in progress to track down the militants. The entire area has been cordoned off, he said, adding that there were three to five militants involved in the attack.

Meanwhile, Army officials attribute the sudden spurt in militants activities to the rise in infiltration from across the Line of Control.

Heading: ATS on trail of key SIMI activist - Indian Express
Content:
The Army has started investigating how militants managed to successfully ambush an Army convoy on the Srinagar-Baramulla highway on Saturday evening, despite sophisticated jammers—supposed deterrents to explosives since they block all electronic devices with a certain reach — that were moving with it. The Improvised Explosive Device (IED) attack on the convoy left 10 soldiers dead and 17 others injured.

To prevent Army convoys from being attacked by powerful IED and car bomb attacks, the military had recently started moving jammers with them.

Brigadier K A Muthanna who was the first senior Army commander to reach on the spot told The Indian Express that it is extremely difficult to prevent such attacks, since they are meticulously planned. "A lot of planning has gone into this attack and every aspect is being examined," he said. Defence spokesperson, Lt Col Anil Mathur added the investigations were on taken up to evaluate how militants managed to target the convoy in the presence of jammers. "One possibility is that militants might have manually triggered the powerful IED as the convoy was passing on the highway," he said and added, "all possibilities are being explored by the Army experts. Mathur said that due to the road-widening activity on the highway, there was a movement of road workers and vehicles. "It's here that the militants seem to have managed to divert attention of the Road Opening Party (ROP) and planted the IED in a mound of earth."

Every day, 10 to 20 army convoys move on the highways and roads of Kashmir from different bases up to the Line of Control. But even though the Army recently procured dozens of jammers to travel along with them, the devices are not invincible — officials in the Army and police say that instead of electronic devices, the militants used the manual-wire technique to trigger the IED.

Heading: Naveen announces land for families of slain jawans - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) is trying to ascertain the whereabouts of a Mira Road resident Abdul Subhan Qureshi, allegedly an important SIMI activist responsible for arranging finances for the hardline faction of the organisation. His name was recently disclosed by Safdar Nagori and Shibly Peedical Abdul, the all-India and South India chiefs respectively of the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), while being grilled by ATS investigators.

Nagori and Shibly were subjected to narco-analysis tests at the Kalina Forensic Sciences Laboratory on Saturday afternoon. Both are currently lodged at Arthur Road Jail.

"While being questioned on the organisation's sources of finance, the arrested accused named one Abdul Subhan Qureshi, who is a Mira Road resident. According to the accused, Qureshi holds the post of treasurer, and is responsible for collection of funds for the hardline faction of the SIMI. Most of these finances were obtained through donations," Additional Commissioner of Police (ATS) Parambir Singh told The Indian Express.

According to the ATS, Qureshi has a previous criminal record but was never under the scanner for terrorist activities. The ATS is now trying to locate his whereabouts, as he has gone underground after news of Nagori's and Shibly's arrest broke.

"Qureshi was also supposed to attend the high-level meeting of SIMI activists on July 6, 2006 at a densely forested place near Ujjain. However, he cancelled his plans of attending the meeting two days prior to it. Records show that he was arrested by Kurla police in 1999 in a case of defacement of property. However, he has never been booked by the ATS before under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act. He has gone underground, and further investigations are on in the matter," said Singh.

The police will also probe the possibility of Qureshi having been in touch with 7/11 serial blasts accused Rizwaan Mohammed Dawrey, who allegedly sent funds from Riyadh through the hawala network to Lashkar-e-Toiba's (LeT) western India chief Faizal Shaikh in Mumbai, at the behest of LeT commander Azam Cheema. There is an Interpol Red Corner Notice against Dawrey.

"Narco-analysis tests are being conducted on Nagori and Shibly, and we hope to get a lot of information from this. They might divulge crucial information on their possible involvement in the 7/11 and Malegaon serial blasts, as well as give more information on their associates," said Singh.

Heading: Muslim girls benefit from govt scholarship schemes - Indian Express
Content: Four days after the killing of 17 policemen in the Malkangiri blast by Naxalites, Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on Sunday announced land for the families of the killed jawans. Naveen, who has asked Director General of Police G C Nanda to probe the Malkangiri blast within a month, handed over cheques of Rs four lakh to the families of the slain jawans after paying homage at the Martyrs' pillar. The CM also announced that plots would be provided to each family for building houses besides a government job to one person from the family. Naveen promised to consider the demand of special allowance for those deployed in the Naxal-hit areas. He added that manpower shortage in the force would be removed through fresh recruitments.

Heading: Remote Bastar Judum relief camp hit by ailments - Indian Express
Content:
The UPA Government may be still grappling with the 'Muslim factor' in the Nuclear Deal. But it can be proud of one thing — the girl students in the minority communities are surging ahead like never before, courtesy its various minorities-friendly initiatives.

The annual assessment carried out by the Government for the year 2007-08 has found that girls have bagged around 62 per cent of the various scholarship schemes initiated by the Minorities Ministry last year; 67 per cent of the scholarships in the case of the merit-cum-means scheme have gone to girls while it is 58 per cent in the case of the post-matric scholarships.

As per the data, the Muslim community has secured 72.7 per cent of the total scholarships while Christians and Sikhs have secured 17.55 per cent and 6.54 per cent, respectively. Gender-wise break up of scholarships availed gives a more encouraging picture which defies many conventional perceptions. In the case of the Muslim community, girls have bagged 61 per cent of the post-matric scholarships sanctioned in 2007 while boys have got only 39 per cent. It is 63 per cent and 37 per cent in the case of the Christian community and 30.48 and 69.52 per cent in the Sikh community.

"The annual assessment carried out by the Ministry has been an eye opener for even us. We never expected this kind of a turnaround. If we are able to sustain this momentum for a while, then there is no stopping the girls," said the official concerned.

The most important significance of these figures, according to the official, is the fact that these scholarships are meant for higher education. "If girls have secured more than 60 per cent of the scholarships for higher education, then it means there will be more women professionals from the minority communities," he said. What adds more sheen to the whole affair is the fact that all these scholarships are awarded purely on the basis of merit, he added.

It may be recalled that the Sachar Committee report had stated that the graduation rate amongst Muslims was only 5 per cent — 12 per cent among males and 6 per cent among females in urban areas; 5 per cent for males and only 1 per cent for females in rural areas.

Heading: Sarpanch killed by Maoists - Indian Express
Content:
Diseases have struck an anti-Naxal Salwa Judum relief camp at the south Bastar region of Dantewada district in Chhattisgarh. A large number of tribals are suffering from viral fever, malaria, diarrhoea and skin ailments at the remote Jagargunda camp — the only one among 23 such camps where even food supplies have to be airlifted owing to security reasons.

Security personnel who returned from duty at the camp informed the authorities about the health ailments being faced by the 2,700 inmates living there.

"Some 400 children are the worst-affected. Almost all of them are suffering from skin diseases such as itching, fungal infections and lesions. There is a shortage of common medicines and even soaps," said sources in the police, adding that "MBBS doctors seldom visit this camp apparently due to security concerns".

Dantewada district collector S P Sori, too, admitted, "Jagargunda is different from other camps in the sense that it is not easily accessible. Sori told The Indian Express that an ayurvedic doctor regularly visited the camp and two trained health workers were also available there.

"Adequate stock of medicines and essentials such as soaps and oil are supplied whenever a helicopter is available," he said, adding, "Despite problems, steps are being taken to provide necessary healthcare facilities at the camp."

Tribals belonging to the nearby villages have been given shelter at the camp in Jagargunda sub-tehsil, which is around 130 km from the Dantewada district headquarters. Road access to the area has been a challenge in view of the possibility of Maoist ambushes and landmine explosions.

On many occasions in the past three years, food stocks exhausted at the camp. Three months ago, 10 truckloads of food stock that were sent to Jagargunda from Dornapal, under heavy escort of Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), took almost two days to cover a distance of 70 km safely.

According to official figures, as many as 56,675 people belonging to 459 villages are living in the 23 relief camps set up in Naxalite-infested Dantewada and Bijapur districts in Bastar ever since they deserted their native villages following threats from Maoists three years ago.

The trouble began in June 2005 when locals launched Salwa Judum, a movement against the Naxalites, aimed at urging people to stay away from Maoists and also to isolate the rebels in the villages. The Naxalites retaliated by unleashing violence against those participating in Judum meetings, forcing them to seek shelter in these camps.

Heading: 20 missing Indians appear before NZ immigration dept - Indian Express
Content:
A BJP leader and village panchayat sarpanch was shot by Maoist rebels, who stormed his house, set ablaze his tractor, looted cash and food grains at Bastnar, about 40 km from Bastar district headquarters in Jagdalpur late on Saturday.

Police sources said the Naxalites entered into the house and shot Sarpanch Gangruram Kashyap (48) from point blank range. They looted cash, foodgrain stock and also took away his cattle .

Security personnel on Sunday carried out a combing operation in the nearby areas following the incident. This was the first incident of a Naxalite attack in the area. It is suspected that the rebels, who had reportedly formed a new Bastnar division of CPI (Maoist) recently, were trying to spread their base in the area.

Meanwhile, Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committee member Avdesh Kumar Gautam had a narrow escape near Nakulnar weekly market in Dantewara when the Maoists missed their target while opening fire on him.

Gautam, who is on the hit list of Maoists because of his close association with Salwa Judum leaders, has been provided security cover.

Heading: Tribal kids to get free English-medium education in new Chhattisgarh scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty Indian Catholic pilgrims, who had gone missing in New Zealand's capital Auckland during a stopover while going to Sydney, appeared before the New Zealand Immigration Department on Saturday. They said they were brought to that country with a promise of settling permanently.

The youths were part of a group of 39 persons, most of them Punjabis, who had gone to Sydney to see the Pope at the "World Youth Day Celebrations". They said they had paid Rs 5-8 lakh to various travel agents of Punjab and Delhi to join this trip and were given a month's visa to participate in the Pope's function.

Daljit Singh, a spokesman of the New Zealand Sikh Society, said two high-level teams were formed to investigate the racket in both New Zealand and India. The teams would also examine the role of some church officials in the racket.

The 20 youths had given their statements to the department, as they were afraid that their visas would be cancelled. The remaining 19 youths, who were still missing, had been told to report by Tuesday, or their visas would be revoked, Daljit added.

Among the seven missing youths from Bholath, two have reported back: Sandeep, an electrician, and Rup Lal, a former sarpanch of Kala Bagarian. Sandeep said their group included three Hindu and two Muslim youths from Delhi.

Daljit said the trip was meant for the Christian community, and foul play was evident from the inclusion of some youths of other communities.

Seven youths from Bholath, six from Lamma Pind, Jalandhar, and about 10 youths from Sansarpur, Dheena and Sofi villages have also gone missing. They have not contacted their families since they left on July 5. Their families said they were not aware of their whereabouts and did not know whether they would come back.

Rup Lal informed the Immigration Department that they were told to live in Toranga in NZ, where there were many Indians. They were asked not to get in touch with their relatives so that their whereabouts would not be revealed.

Later in the evening, two more youths surrendered to the department. Their names have not been revealed yet.

Daljit said they were taking up the case of the youths, because they belonged to poor families in Punjab. "We want to present the case of these youths properly before the department, so that they get a good hearing and sufficient time to put in their appeals."

Father George Waraich, secretary to the Bishop had on Friday said that some Delhi-based agency had been contacted by Father Peter of the Jalandhar Diocese to arrange this trip.

The boys had given an affidavit that they would come back by July 24.

Heading: 10 Youth League activists held for killing headmaster - Indian Express
Content:
In an ambitious scheme, 125 children belonging to the most poverty-stricken and backward tribal communities of two districts of Chhattisgarh have been enrolled for free education in prominent schools in Raipur starting this academic year.

As many as 35 private English-medium schools have already come forward to 'adopt' five children each every year under the scheme, named 'Udan' (flight), and will provide free education as well as food and accommodation to students belonging to the

Kamar, Bhunjia and Baiga tribes from the remote forest areas of Raipur and Kawardha districts.

The beneficiaries were selected on the basis of their performance in screening tests organised by the schools in the tribal areas of Gariaband, Mainpur, Chhura and Devbhog in Raipur district and in Kawardha. Children studying in Classes I to VIII were eligible to compete for the opportunity.

Claiming that 'Udan' was the only scheme of its kind, Raipur district collector Sonmani Bora, who is coordinating the implementation of the project, asserted that parents are "enthusiastic that they can send their children to schools in the state capital".

He also said a tripartite agreement would be signed between the district administration, the school management committee and the institution adopting the child to ensure that each student would continue to receive similar facilities till the completion of their schooling.

In addition, said Bora, a proposal has been forwarded to the state Government to provide funds for other children from these backward communities so that no child was deprived of the opportunity to pursue a higher standard of education.

Talking about the source of funds, he said a separate corpus would be created with a share from the district administration's brisk scheme, the Kamar and Bhunjia development authority and contributions from the public.

Bora said a proposal was also being sent to the Human Resource Development Ministry, requesting it to earmark at least five per cent seats in Chhattisgarh's Navodaya Vidyalayas and Kendriya Vidyalayas for children belonging to these "most backward" tribal communities.

Heading: Police protection off, siblings on the run from mom’s killers - Indian Express
Content:
Ten activists of Youth League, the youth wing of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), were taken into custody by the Kerala police on Sunday in connection with the death of a headmaster in Malappuram district. The primary school headmaster, James Augustine, was killed during an attack on a school on Saturday by some Youth League activists, seeking withdrawal of a textbook.

Tension prevailed at many places in Malappuram and Kozhikode, which observed a dawn-to-dusk shutdown called by the CPI-M-led Left Democratic Front. All Left-affiliated organisations of government employees and teachers have decided to go on strike on Monday to protest the headmaster's death.

Preliminary autopsy report suggests that James suffered grievous injuries on his head and other parts of the body.

Heading: Court declares UP minister absconder - Indian Express
Content:
For the last six months, eight-year-old Shivani and her seven-year-old brother Sanskar have been on the run. They had witnessed the murder of their mother who was killed in a property dispute. But the police have now withdrawn their security, leaving them exposed to the threat from their mother's killers.

The children are being taken care of by their cousin Somesh Kumar. He keeps changing the location of the children to protect them. They are scared of going to their own home at Char Bagh ever since the security was withdrawn last January.

"Two constables were deployed at the house. They were withdrawn a day before Moharrum as the police station needed more men to make arrangements in view of the festival," said prosecution counsel Akhilesh Awasthi. "The case is sensitive as the children had identified the killers in front of the magistrate. Later, the court rejected the bail application of the five accused," he added.

"We can't provide anyone permanent security without a directive from the state Government. The local beat in-charge and constables have been asked to regularly check on them," said Superintendent of Police (West) Paresh Pandey.

Meena Sonkar was killed on December 18 last year at her home. Her husband, who had a serious kidney problem, died the next day.

Ironically, Meena had written to various police authorities about the threat to her life a week before she was killed, but they did not pay attention. Now her children have been left unprotected.

The children had identified Mayur Sonkar, Manish Sonkar, Ram Babu, Mayank Sonkar and Sabli Sonkar, who were arrested for the crime and sent to jail. Now the associates of these men are after the life of the children. Not only are they eyewitnesses to the crime, they also inherit the property which was the subject of the dispute.

"The children are leading a traumatic life as the associates of the accused have been threatening them to retract their statement," said Somesh, "besides, they are losing on education. I have just changed their school."

Somesh said he had written several times to the DGP, the SSP of Lucknow and the Human Rights Commission to arrange security for them but to no avail.

Heading: Woman crushed to death by Blueline bus - Indian Express
Content:
A fatehpur court has issued an order for the attachment of property of UP Sports Minister Ayodhya Prasad Pal, after he failed to appear in a case of attempt to murder despite several summons. A non-bailable warrant (NBW) against the minister has also been pending for long.

Confirming the development, Assistant Prosecuting Officer RK Tiwari said that the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Kamlesh Dubey had fixed August 4 for the next hearing.

Ayodhya Prasad Pal alleged that he had been framed in the case by the previous government. "They were pressurising me to join their party. When I did not agree, they booked me in a false case", said the minister.

The case against Pal and three others was registered at Malawa police station in Fatehpur on December 6, 2003.

In his complaint, Bhagat Singh Rana stated that Pal and others had been trying to capture 26 bigha land of the village by preparing fake papers. When the villagers objected, Pal and his associates opened fire on them, injuring two people.

After the BSP Government came to power, it moved for withdrawal of the case, but the CJM rejected the application. About two months ago, the state Government appealed in the Allahabad High Court against the CJM's order.

Fatehpur Superintendent of Police K S Pipil said the Government's application for the withdrawal of the case was rejected by the CJM because of a technical error.

"The withdrawal application was moved after the complainant and all four witnesses submitted an affidavit in the court stating that they were pressurised by the previous government to register the case against Pal and others", said Pal's lawyer Tariq Fareedi.

Heading: No snapping ties with Iran, says Antony - Indian Express
Content: In a second accident involving a Blueline bus, a 60-year-old woman was crushed to death in Nand Nagri area of northeast Delhi on Sunday. Police said the incident took place around 12. 30 pm at Mandawali crossing. The victim was crushed by the bus plying on route number 279, between Anand Vihar and Janhangirpuri. "The woman was standing on the footboard of the bus. When the driver accelerated, she lost her balance, fell down and was crushed under the rear wheels of the bus. The driver of the bus, identified as Purushottam Kumar, has been arrested," said a police official. The bus has been impounded and a case registered against the driver.

Heading: Nepal party to raise Arushi case in House - Indian Express
Content:
Defence Minister A K Antony on Sunday said India would "react strongly" if the US initiated military action against Iran.

Addressing the media on the sidelines of an air show organised by the Southern Air Command here, Antony said the country had not changed its policy towards Iran. "India would not snap long-established international relations. There is no going back on this front."

He said the Congress would not water down its independent policy. "Nuclear energy is essential for the country's growing energy requirements. It is unfortunate that it is being depicted as anti-Muslim," he said.

Exuding confidence that the UPA Government would win the confidence motion, the Congress leader said the CPI-M will have to "pay a heavy price for joining hands with communal forces".

"The CPI-M and other Left parties have have stooped to the level of embracing even Devil to bring down the Government. To oust the UPA, the Left parties have sought the support of forces which they have been opposing for several years. We have seen the CPI-M general secretary rushing to Mayawati's house," Antony said.

Heading: Kuldeep Bishnoi at NDA dinner - Indian Express
Content:
Claiming that the two Nepalese nationals arrested in connection with the Arushi murder case in India were falsely implicated, a local political party here has said it would raise the issue in the Himalayan nation's Parliament.

Rastriya Jana Morcha (RJM) chairman Chitra Bahadur K C said his party, which has four members in the House, would take up the issue of the arrest of Krishna Thapa and Raj Kumar in Parliament.

RJM's general secretary and former Parliament member Dilaram Acharya alleged that a conspiracy was hatched by the CBI to give Rajesh Talwar, Arushi's father and an accused in the case, a clean chit.

Heading: Poor students suffer the most as schools lack basic infrastructure - Indian Express
Content:
Rebel Congress leader and MP Kuldeep Bishnoi attended the dinner hosted by the NDA here on Sunday. "I have decided to vote against the UPA Government but as for joining the NDA is concerned, I will decide later," said Bishnoi.

He said he would like to see L K Advani as the next Prime Minister of India. "I want to see Advani as the next Prime Minister. I am highly impressed with his style of functioning. I think he will be the best for the country," said the son of former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal.

He also claimed that he was approached by a person "very close" to him with a Rs 100-crore offer to abstain during the trust vote. "On Friday evening, I was approached with an offer of Rs 100 crore to abstain from the trust vote. I was also offered a ministership in return of supporting the nuclear deal."

Another Independent MP from Uttar Pradesh Harish Nagpal was also there while there were reports that a couple of Akali MPs could not make it to the NDA dinner.

Heading: A 24-Karat affair - Indian Express
Content: While there is speculation in political circles about Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee not contesting a parliamentary election again, his detractors in the Left camp say the incumbent Speaker actually has no constituency to contest from. Bolpur, which he represented several times in Parliament, has become a reserved constituency after the delimitation exercise. Chatterjee used to contest from Jadavpur but had shifted to Bolpur after losing to Mamata Banerjee in 1984. Jadavpur is now represented by the CPI(M)'s Sujan Chakraborty. "His differences with the party leadership could become a big stumbling block in getting a new constituency. No wonder he is not interested in contesting again," said a Left leader.

Heading: Somnath stands tall while CPM gets the villain tag - Indian Express
Content: When the Politburo of the CPI(M) met here on July 8 to take the all-important decision of withdrawing support to the UPA Government, it was more or less a family affair. Only three members attended the meeting — the party's first couple Prakash and Brinda Karat, and CITU leader M K Pandhe, who is lying low these days after the party boxed him in for his comments that Muslims are opposed to the nuclear deal. While Sitaram Yechury was abroad, S Ramachandran Pillai was in Chennai to pay homage to senior comrade P Ramachandran, who had died a day earlier.

Heading: Bastion bristles at IUML ‘pro-US’ stand - Indian Express
Content:
Somnathbabu has become our hero for the strong stand he has taken against the party. But his party has become the villain in the perception of our community. Till now, we used to think they are secular. The mask has now fallen," said an angry Muhammed Mohsin, the middle-aged headmaster of Chunpalasi High school in Illambazar that falls in Somnath Chatterjee's Lok Sabha constituency of Bolpur. Chatterjee's contribution of Rs two lakh from the MP fund helped the school building come up in 2001.

As the fate of the UPA Government hangs in the balance with Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee occupying centerstage, the fallout of the developments in Delhi have touched this far-away constituency in a big way. Chatterjee's popularity has soared while that of the party has evidently nosedived. Voters have begun questioning the CPI(M)'s secular credentials.

After being defeated by Mamata Banerjee in Jadavpur constituency in 1984, Chatterjee switched to Bolpur where he defeated former Congress CM Siddhartha Shankar Ray in 1985, after the death of the sitting MP. Bolpur has returned him to the Lok Sabha in every election since then. If Chatterjee's words are any indication, he is going to call it a day and would not enter the electoral arena any more.

"Ever since he became the Speaker, he stopped visiting the party office in Bolpur; not only in Bolpur, but elsewhere too, on principle," said Chatterjee's pointsman in Bolpur CPI(M) party office, Hirendranath Ghosh.

Ghosh went on to add, "He had become the Speaker by unanimous choice, not as a CPI(M) MP. I am all for party diktats, but people's sentiments should be respected as well."

Bolpur has 30 per cent Muslim voters. At the grassroots level, comrades are finding it difficult to answer some tough questions being put to them.

"I have spoken to the Speaker even today over phone," added Ghosh as he showed a letter he had received from Chatterjee's office regarding setting up of a bank in Bahiri village near Bolpur. "He still finds time to address public grievances," said Ghosh.

Sheikh Kamal, zonal committee member of Illambazar, a Muslim-dominated block under Bolpur, looked frustrated, sitting in the his office in Ghurisha where his party lost in the panchayat elections to Siddiqullah Choudhuri-led PDCI, a couple of months back. "Already, in the last panchayat elections, a section of the Muslims turned against us. Moreover, if we finally vote along with the BJP against the UPA, our reputation as an anti-communalism party will be under threat. It was very hard for us to build our secular image at the grassroots level and now we have to face the music from the villagers," Kamal said.

From local farmers to intellectuals in Santiniketan, people voiced their anguish against the CPI(M) and for their Speaker MP. For octogenarian Bhobotosh Datta, who was Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's professor of Bengali at Presidency College in the 60s, it is Somnath and not the CPI(M) who matters.

"Everybody here wants Somnath to stay on as the Speaker and also as our MP. I would have never voted for the CPI(M) but for Somnath. He maintains a great degree of neutrality. I have seen him from close quarters. He looks after everybody, irrespective of political affiliations," said Dutta.

Bolpur Constituency

Total population 15,00,000

Total number of electorates 10, 35,012

Muslim population 31 per cent

In 2004 Lok Sabha elections, Somnath Chatterjee got 5,04,836, Nirmal Majhi of TMC got 1,94,531, Dhananjoy Ghosh of the Congress got 48,756

Heading: Confused over anti-deal posture, Advani’s voters seek other issues - Indian Express
Content:
The anti-US sentiment is fast eating into the Muslim community in this coastal constituency, represented by Minister of State for External Affairs E Ahamed. While Ahamed and his party, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), have many reasons to back the Congress over the nuclear deal, Muslims in this League bastion, cutting across their political affiliation, could hardly stomach 'India giving in to the US'.

Ordinary Muslims, whom The Indian Express met in select parts of the constituency, feel that the deal would help America establish its hegemony over India and at a later stage, over Arab nations.

"America is not a suitable partner for us. They had killed Saddam and have always supported the anti-Islamic stand of Israel," says Ummer, a fisherman.

"Confusion prevails at the grassroots level over IUML's stand on the issue. Many feel that party has not made up its mind, though the general trend in the past elections had been to obey the party's official line," observes Ahamed Kutty, secretary, Maunathul Islam Association (MIA), Ponnani. MIA trains Muslim converts.

"The community feels that the deal is anti-Indian. If the issue keeps burning till the next election, it might influence the voting behaviour of Muslims," says E V Abdurahiman at Edappal. He has recently returned from the Gulf.

However, IUML's Ponnani constituency president Asharaf Kokkoor said that raising anti-US feeling has been an election strategy of the CPI(M). "This time, we would see the community is not carried away by that sentiment," he added.

Political observers say the IUML is almost silent on the issue, while the other camp, comprising the PDP, NDF and Jama'at Islami, has been actively campaigning to keep the community abreast of the latest developments and nurture anti-US sentiments.

Solidarity, the youth wing of Jama'at Islami, has been campaigning against imperialism. The League's stand on the issue has given a fillip to the outfit's efforts to mobilise anti-US opinion in the community.

Muslims in the region, known for their orthodoxy and religiosity, had en bloc voted for the IUML in the past. The party's failure to address developmental concerns of the constituency had never influenced the voters. The late G M Banatwala had won from Ponnani with huge margins and with little legwork.

However, this time, the party has many things to worry about. Educated Muslim youths harbour strong anti-US sentiments. Many of them are easy targets for the NDF, PDP and Jama'at Islami.
